identity.title: ALMA Observations of the Protostellar Disk around the VeLLO IRAS 16253-2429

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA long-baseline observations toward the Class 0 protostar IRAS 16253-2429 (hereafter IRAS 16253) with a resolution down to 0.12$''$ ($\sim$15 au).

question.value: Is there a disk around the VeLLO IRAS 16253, and what are its dust, kinematic and chemical (CO freeze-out) properties?

evidence.quote: We aim to search for a disk around this unique source and study its physical and chemical properties.
(Cycle 4 project, 2016.1.00598.S)
we obtained 0.87 mm data from the ALMA archive (2015.1.00741.S, PI: L. Looney)
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00598.S, 2013.1.00879.S, and 2015.1.00741.S.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: channel width 122 kHz (0.16 km/s) CO, 61 kHz (0.08 km/s) C18O

evidence.quote: The channel width was 122 kHz (0.16 km s$^{-1}$) for CO ($2-1$) and 61 kHz (0.08 km s$^{-1}$) for C$^{18}$O ($2-1$).
simultaneously observe CO ($2-1$), C$^{18}$O ($2-1$), and dust continuum emission at 217 GHz
simultaneously observe CO ($2-1$), C$^{18}$O ($2-1$), and dust continuum emission at 217 GHz
The continuum bandwidth was 1840 MHz, centered at 217 GHz (1.38 mm).
The data were obtained in configuration of C40-7 with a projected baseline range of 11 to 2629 k$\lambda$
resulting in a spatial resolution of $0.11\ensuremath{''}\times0.08\ensuremath{''}$ with uniform weighting for the continuum

evidence.quote: The rms noise level is 0.066 mJy beam$^{-1}$ for the continuum map, and 5.6 and 4.9 mJy beam$^{-1}$ for the CO and C$^{18}$O maps
The total observing time was 48 min and the on-source time was $\approx$20 min.
on 2017 Aug 18th (Cycle 4 project, 2016.1.00598.S)

analysis_steps.goal: Fit continuum visibilities with double Gaussian

method.value: Double Gaussian fit to visibility amplitudes at 0.87 and 1.38 mm, finding a break at ~200 kλ between extended and compact components

evidence.loc: continuum emission at 0.87 mm and 1.38 mm
evidence.quote: We employ a double Gaussian fit to the observed amplitude but not phase, and we find a break point at a $uv$-distance of $\approx$200 k$\lambda$

validation.value: Check sources compared to reference positions (within 10 mas at 1.3 mm, 5 mas at 0.87 mm)

evidence.loc: continuum emission at 0.87 mm and 1.38 mm
evidence.quote: find that they are consistent with the referenced positions within 10 mas and 5 mas, respectively

analysis_steps.goal: Model continuum offset with radiative transfer

method.value: RADMC-3D flared disk (A) and torus-like thick disk (B1/B2) grids, chi2 fit to visibilities beyond 200 kλ using vis_sample

evidence.quote: We construct model grids (Sections [4.1.1](#sec:modA) and [4.1.2](#sec:modB)) to perform a $\chi^2$ fitting to the visibilities at uv-distances beyond 200 k$\lambda$.

key_parameters.value: Model A free parameters: Lstar, Mdisk, Rdisk, theta_flared, a_pow, a_max; r0 = 25 au

evidence.quote: We take six free parameters including the protostellar luminosity ($L_{\rm star}$), $M_{\rm disk}$ (total mass of the disk scaled by $\Sigma_0$), $R_{\rm disk}$, $\theta_{\rm flared}$, $a_{\rm pow}$, and $a_{\rm max}$.

assumptions.value: Inclination 65 deg from Gaussian aspect ratio; center, PA fixed from 1.38 mm fit; grain size distribution n(a) ∝ a^-a_pow

evidence.quote: an inclination angle of $65\ensuremath{^\circ}$ is estimated from the Gaussian aspect ratio

fitting.value: chi-squared grid fit; errors from chi2 distribution at 99.9% confidence

evidence.quote: The error of the fitted parameters are calculated with the $\chi^2$ distribution in a confidence level of 99.9%.

validation.value: Compare model peak offset with observed 46 mas

evidence.quote: the offset (7 mas) in this model is still much smaller than the observed one (46 mas)

method.value: Rotating infalling envelope model with conserved angular momentum and free-fall, LTE radiative transfer, chi2 over major and minor axis PV cuts

evidence.quote: We model the PV diagrams assuming a rotating infalling envelope with conservation of angular momentum.

software: Lee et al. 2014 radiative transfer code

key_parameters.value: Free: rho0, p, theta_flared, V_rot,0, V_infall,0, F_C18O; C18O fit at |V-Vlsr|<1.6 km/s, CO at >1.6 km/s

evidence.quote: $\mid V-V_{\rm lsr} \mid<1.6$ km s$^{-1}$ for C$^{18}$O and $\mid V-V_{\rm lsr} \mid>1.6$ km s$^{-1}$ for CO
We take the CO abundance relative to H$_2$ as $X_{\rm CO}=5\times10^{-4}$ and the C$^{18}$O isotopic ratio of $X_{\rm CO}/X_{\rm C^{18}O}=560$ (cite: wi94).

fitting.value: chi-squared minimization; modeled images convolved with the beam

evidence.quote: we convolve the modeled images with the beam of the observations and make the PV diagrams with the same PV cuts

analysis_steps.goal: CO channel-map model with CO depletion

method.value: Compare best-fit dynamic model with channel maps via vis_sample, per-channel intensity scaling, add f_snow zeroing gas below f_snow×H

evidence.loc: CO channel map and CO-depletion model
evidence.quote: the gas density at $z<f_{\rm snow}\times H(R)$ is set to zero, with $f_{\rm snow}$ between 0 (no CO depletion) and 1 (complete CO depletion)

fitting.value: best f_snow = 0.55, chi2_r 1.78 vs 1.92 for f_snow=0

evidence.loc: CO channel map and CO-depletion model
evidence.quote: we find the best-fit CO-depletion model for $f_{\rm snow}=0.55$ with $\chi^2_{\rm r}=1.78$ while $\chi^2_{\rm r}=1.92$ for $f_{\rm snow}=0$

validation.value: Qualitative reproduction of quadruple pattern; chi2 difference small

evidence.loc: CO channel map and CO-depletion model
evidence.quote: The model with CO depletion reproduces the quadruple pattern qualitatively well, though the CO peak positions are not perfectly matched and the difference between the $\chi^2_{\rm r}$ is small.

claims.hypothesis: The compact continuum component traces a disk
claims.experiment: Double Gaussian visibility fit at two wavelengths
claims.result: Consistent PA and aspect ratio, minor axis aligned with outflow
claims.finding: Compact component likely traces a disk

evidence.loc: continuum emission at 0.87 mm and 1.38 mm
evidence.quote: Therefore, the compact component likely traces a disk.

claims.hypothesis: The 0.87/1.38 mm offset comes from optical depth differences
claims.result: Models give 7-20 mas offsets vs 46 mas observed
claims.finding: Optical depth can contribute but does not fully explain it

evidence.quote: Our model does generate an offset of $10-20$ mas, but it is still smaller than the observed value.

claims.hypothesis: A Keplerian disk is present and formed from a first core
claims.experiment: PV and channel map modeling of CO and C18O
claims.result: Centrifugal radii 16-64 au give Keplerian disk radius of 8-32 au
claims.finding: Disk too large for slow-start growth, favoring early-start

evidence.quote: Together with the size from the dust continuum, we speculate that a Keplerian disk is present with a radius of $8-32$ au in IRAS 16253.

claims.hypothesis: CO freeze-out explains the quadruple CO pattern
claims.experiment: Add f_snow depletion to channel map model
claims.finding: CO depletion plausible but not uniquely established

evidence.loc: freeze out of CO in the protostellar disk
evidence.quote: CO depletion is considered as the most plausible explanation for the quadruple pattern in the channel maps although the other hypotheses cannot be completely ruled out.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Proper motion and phase calibration error as causes of the offset were considered but not excluded; dust absorption and CO self-absorption rejected for the quadruple pattern

evidence.loc: CO channel map and CO-depletion model
evidence.quote: The second hypothesis is also unlikely because the far side (or bottom side) should be much fainter than the near side by being obscured.

limitations_admitted.value: Offset smaller than beam; calibration issue or proper motion not excluded

evidence.loc: grain growth at the Class 0 stage
